subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, the braids are rendering as long orange-gold tubes hanging from the head down the chest, which looks off since the HAIR paint's gradient makes them appear like stripes rather than natural hair.

I should darken the braid colour to something like a dark cord or leather tone, shorten them, and push them outward along x so they stop overlapping the face and jaw from the front view.

For the staff, the skull's glowing eyes sit like green blobs on the sides rather than proper eye sockets, which reads oddly in the side view, though the front view and horns look fine. The staff position in the right hand seems acceptable.

I'm also noting the troll's head looks too small relative to the body.

For the back fetish rack, in the side view the bone column appears detached and floating away from the body instead of resting against the back. I need to compute the torso's back-facing z-coordinate at different heights and move the rods closer, roughly matching the back curve around z -0.15 to -0.2 at that height.

I'll nudge the rack to z -0.16 and pull the skull in to -0.05. The small loose decorative parts near the hips look fine, and the troll's stance and arm placement from the front also read okay despite being a bit spread out.

Checking the other small details — stirring stick, mud, hands, pauldron, staff — they all seem fine as placed. The main issue I'm settling on is the troll's eyes reading too tiny and glowing amber; I want to enlarge them from 0.028 radius to about 0.036 along with the brow, since the face overall looks undersized and scaling the whole head seems like too many edits.

The tusks need real attention too — they're the character's key identifying feature and currently too small, hidden by braids and barely visible. I'm planning to thicken and lengthen them, curving upward more dramatically, while also cleaning up some dead placeholder code and an unnecessary early surface call that's just wasted computation. The staff skull's glowing green eyes and the mohawk both check out fine as-is.

I want to add some visual flourish — maybe a chest rune glow, though I'll skip that for now — and sprinkle in a few floating glowing wisps or fireflies around the figure for atmosphere, cheaply implemented as glowing spheres. The troll's overall proportions check out against its staff height. Now I'm reworking the braid geometry, shifting the curve outward and adjusting its color and position along the head.

Adjusting braid curve coordinates...

Now I'm turning to the tusks, which need the bezier path edited in both places it appears in the code since the path gets rebuilt.

Good, that confirms the match is unique. Now I'm planning to replace the entire tusk block as one unit, then move on to defining the glowing amber eyes using geometry placed relative to the head.

I still need to adjust the eye socket size and position, pull the back rack rods forward to avoid clipping into the skull, remove placeholder elements, and sequence the firefly effects before the rest pose. I'll make these edits carefully one at a time.
